data.q: Which command is used to publish a Cloudflare Worker from the command line using Wrangler?
data.e: The official CLI tool Wrangler uses the `wrangler deploy` command to upload and publish a Worker.

data.q: In a wrangler.toml file, which field defines the name of the script that will be executed for a Worker?
data.e: The `main` field points to the JavaScript/TypeScript file that contains the Worker code.

data.q: What is the default route pattern applied when you bind a Worker to a zone without specifying a route?
o: No route – the Worker must be triggered manually
data.e: If you publish a Worker without a custom route, it defaults to the catch‑all pattern `/*` for the specified zone.

data.q: Which Cloudflare feature allows a Worker to access KV storage with low latency at the edge?
data.e: Workers KV (Key‑Value) is a globally replicated, low‑latency storage solution designed for Workers.

data.q: When using Wrangler, which command generates a new Worker project skeleton?
data.e: `wrangler generate <name>` scaffolds a new Worker project with a starter template.

data.q: How can you restrict a Worker to only run on HTTP POST requests using the request method in the script?
data.e: The HTTP method is available via `request.method`; compare it to the string "POST".

data.q: Which of the following is NOT a supported language/runtime for Cloudflare Workers?
data.e: Workers run on V8 and can execute WebAssembly modules (e.g., compiled from Rust). Python is not natively supported.

data.q: What environment variable does Wrangler automatically set to indicate the name of the current zone during deployment?
data.e: Wrangler injects `CF_ZONE_ID` (the numeric ID) and `CF_ZONE_NAME` (the domain) into the Worker environment.

data.q: Which Cloudflare product would you pair with Workers to serve static assets with automatic edge caching?
data.e: Cloudflare Pages provides a static site hosting platform that integrates tightly with Workers for edge logic.

data.q: When deploying a Worker to a specific subdomain (e.g., api.example.com), which wrangler.toml property should you set?
data.e: The `routes` array defines URL patterns (including subdomains) that trigger the Worker.

data.q: What is the purpose of the `workers_dev` flag in wrangler.toml?
o: Enable a custom domain for the Worker
Deploy the Worker to a preview subdomain on cloudflare.dev
Allow the Worker to run in development mode locally
Disable Cloudflare analytics for the Worker
data.e: `workers_dev: true` tells Wrangler to publish the Worker to a workers.dev subdomain for testing.

data.q: Which HTTP response header can be set in a Worker to control client‑side caching?
data.e: `Cache-Control` is the standard header to dictate how browsers cache the response.
